en: The Mahāyāna Sūtra of the Noble and Auspicious Dhāraṇī of Lokeśvara, spoken by the Buddha;
translated by the Tripitaka Master and Imperial Preceptor of Nālandā Monastery in Magadha, Central India,
the Purple-Robed Śramaṇa and Subject Fātian.
Translated by Imperial Decree. Thus have I heard.
At one time, the World-Honored One was staying in the country of Kauśāmbī, in the Great Thorny Forest.
He was accompanied by a great assembly of four hundred and fifty bhikṣus,
all of whom were renowned great arhats,
as well as by various bodhisattva-mahāsattvas.
The assemblies of all the Buddhas’ disciples gathered together,
respectfully surrounding [the Buddha] to listen to his teaching of the Dharma.
At that time, there was an elder in the assembly named Moon of Excellence (Candraprabha).
He resided in the great city of Kauśāmbī.
This householder possessed great wisdom and skillful means;
he was surrounded by a full retinue of many sons, daughters, male and female servants, and attendants.
All were endowed with roots of goodness and gave rise to great wholesome minds.
At that time, the elder Sunetra went to visit the World-Honored One; having arrived at the Buddha’s dwelling, he...
With palms joined in reverence, he prostrated at the Buddha’s feet,
circumambulated him a hundred thousand times,
and then withdrew to sit at one side, remaining seated with serene composure.
The elder Candracchattra addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One, today I wish to question the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha."
I now have a matter of doubt within my mind.
I only pray that the World-Honored One, with immeasurable great compassion,
will preach the Dharma for me and untie the knots of my doubts.
At that time, the World-Honored One Śākyamuni addressed the elder Candracchattra, saying:
"I now grant you leave to ask whatever matters you have in mind regarding your doubts."
"You should not harbor such doubts within your own mind.
Having heard what the Buddha had said, the householder Candracchattra addressed the Buddha again, saying, "World-Honored One..."
If good sons or good daughters suffer much poverty,
how can they avoid the suffering of poverty?
"How can those with many illnesses avoid being afflicted by disease? At that time,
the World-Honored One, who possesses all-encompassing wisdom, [spoke].
He addressed the elder Sunetra, saying:
"For what reason do you, being currently impoverished,
harbor doubts in your heart and ask such a question?"
The householder Candra-prabha addressed the Blessed One, saying:
"I am poor now, Blessed One; I am poor now, Sugata.
Yet my home is filled with many kinsmen, sons, daughters, and male and female servants."
Please speak for me now.
World-Honored One, please teach the Dharma in accordance with my question:
by what skillful means can sentient beings who are impoverished be led to leave behind the suffering of poverty?
By what skillful means can sentient beings who are afflicted by many illnesses be freed from disease and suffering?
And how may their provisions, wealth, treasures, grain, barley,
and other such things be made to fill their storehouses?
How may one obtain to see those things one loves and delights in:
gold, silver, mani-jewels, pearls, lapis lazuli,
conch shells, jade, coral, and mother-of-pearl?
May my storehouses of vajra-jewels and the like overflow,
so that my giving may never be exhausted;
how may I obtain a household and a circle of kinsmen?
Having thus addressed the World-Honored One, the elder Sunetra— whether male or female, great or small, noble or sovereign—
spoke these words. At that time:
The Buddha again addressed the householder Moon of Excellence, saying:
"In the past, during incalculable eons ago,
at that time in that world, there was a Buddha who appeared in the world."

He was named the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, Vidyācaraṇasaṃpanna, Sugata, Lokavid, Anuttara, Puruṣadamyasārathi, Śāstā devamanuṣyāṇām, Buddha, Bhagavān, known as the Great Sound of the Vajra-Ocean Holder.
In the presence of that Blessed One,
I shall hear the name of the dhāraṇī called "Auspicious Sustainer of the World.
Having heard this Dharma, I shall constantly uphold, read, recite, and make sincere offerings to it.
Furthermore, you shall extensively expound this dhāraṇī for others.
Son of good family, I now speak this dhāraṇī for you to protect you;
neither humans nor non-humans shall be able to cause you harm.
Yakṣas cannot cause harm; rākṣasas cannot cause harm.
Bhūtas cannot cause harm; piśācas cannot cause harm.
The Piśācas cannot cause harm;
the Kūṣmāṇḍas cannot cause harm;
the Uṣtārakas cannot cause harm; the Bhūtānas cannot cause harm.
The Keṭabhadānava cannot cause harm;
those who feed on excrement cannot cause harm;
those who feed on urine cannot cause harm.
Even if one consumes various kinds of pure or impure things, they cannot cause harm.
Elder Sun-Moon, this Auspicious Dhāraṇī for Sustaining the World—
if there be any son of good family or daughter of good family, [who recites it]...
If one obtains this *dhāraṇī* sūtra within one's own home,
or reverently makes offerings to it while holding it in one's hand,
or contemplates the Dharma of this sūtra with the mind;
Or those who obtain the opportunity to hear this sutra-dharma will then receive,
uphold, read, recite, and make offerings to it;
or they will extensively explain its meaning and purport for others.
These sons and daughters of good family shall always,
day and night, receive protection, peace, and happiness;
their food and drink shall be abundant, and they shall attain great merit and virtue.
If one can wholeheartedly make offerings to this *Śrī-lokadhara-dhāraṇī-sūtra*,
it is equivalent to making offerings to all the Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas of the past, present, and future worlds.
If one can, according to the Dharma, constantly recite this dhāraṇī four times during the middle watch of the night,
this person will cause all the devas to come and provide protection, with joy and delight.
Furthermore, for the sake of this person, [the Tathāgatas] personally descend and rain down sublime,
sweet, and delicious food and drink.
The hosts of devas harbor joy in their hearts toward all the Tathāgatas.
They harbor joy in their hearts toward all the Buddha-dharmas;
they harbor joy in their hearts toward the Buddha’s signless wisdom;
they harbor joy in their hearts toward the harmonious Saṃgha.
With hearts full of joy toward the Dharma-preacher,
the Buddha again addressed the elder Sunetra, saying:
"I now [speak] for your sake and for the sake of all sentient beings in future ages."
May they obtain vast benefit and peace and happiness.
He then spoke this Auspicious Dhāraṇī for Sustaining the World, saying:
*Namo ratnatrayāya namo...* (Homage to the Triple Gem; homage...)

*Svāhā* (23). The Buddha again addressed the elder Candracchattra, saying:
"This Auspicious Dhāraṇī for Sustaining the World possesses great majestic power."
If you are able to maintain and recite this at all times,
no calamities— whether of disease, famine, or untimely death— shall be able to invade you.
Furthermore, if there is anyone who, in their own home or in the home of another, wherever they may be, [maintains it...]
One should make offerings to the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Mahāghoṣa of the Vajradhara Ocean,
and with a sincere heart, maintain the recitation of this Auspicious Dhāraṇī for Upholding the World,
making various kinds of offerings for a full six months.
In this way, whatever matters one aspires to for increase will all be accomplished.

Furthermore, if there is anyone who, according to the ritual, selects a pure location or within a storehouse, establishes a four-sided maṇḍala using white sandalwood incense, and then performs the invocation and offerings to the Tathāgata of Great Sound, the Vajradhara Ocean; [their wishes shall likewise be fulfilled].
And all the Buddhas, the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara, and the assembly of holy beings,
constantly during the night, shall with a sincere mind recite this Auspicious Dhāraṇī for Sustaining the World.
Ensuring that there is no interruption until its accomplishment,
this good man or good woman will immediately obtain the great majestic power of those who bestow blessings and protection.
May all their wishes be fulfilled.
May all wealth, grain, gold, silver, and precious gems be obtained,
and may all fears, obstacles, and disturbances be entirely eliminated.
"Householder Subhacandra, if you are able to diligently receive and uphold this Auspicious World-Sustaining Dhāraṇī,
and can extensively explain it for the sake of others,"
"This will enable you to obtain benefit, welfare, and happiness for a long night among humans and in the heavens.
The householder Sunetra praised him, saying, "Excellent, World-Honored One! You have spoken well.
Thus did the householder Sunetra [behave] toward the World-Honored One.
Having heard this Auspicious World-Upholding Dhāraṇī,
his heart was filled with love and joy, and he leaped for gladness;
with a serene countenance, he prostrated at the Buddha’s feet.
Then he addressed the Buddha, saying: "World-Honored One,
from this day forward, I shall never again forget or lose this Auspicious Dhāraṇī for Sustaining the World."
One should mindfully remember, uphold, read, and recite it;
explain its meaning and make offerings with reverence;
and furthermore, extensively expound this Dharma for others.
At that moment, within the house of the elder Sunetra,
in the brief interval of a finger-snap,
there suddenly appeared various kinds of gold, silver, and precious jewels.
The granaries and treasuries were filled with grain, wheat, and wealth.
At that time, the elder Sunetra gazed upon the World-Honored One without ever averting his eyes,
and he circumambulated him hundreds of thousands of times.
Having prostrated at the Buddha’s feet and completed his salutation, he withdrew.
At that time, the World-Honored One addressed Ānanda, saying:
"Today you should go to the home of the householder Sudatta Candra."
He saw that all his wealth— grain, barley, gold, silver, and precious gems—
filled various vast granaries and treasuries.
At that time, Ānanda, having heard the Buddha’s instruction, [acted accordingly].
He proceeded swiftly to the residence of the householder Candracchattra in the great city of Kauśāmbī;
having arrived, he entered the interior and beheld all the wealth and possessions therein.
The granaries and treasuries were all filled to overflowing with vast quantities of millet, wheat, bushels, and measures of gold, silver,
and various precious gems. At that time, Ānanda suddenly beheld such a sight.
With inward wonder and a smiling countenance,
his heart filled with love, joy, and exultation,
Ānanda then received the Buddha’s instruction.
He then went to where the Buddha was, and upon arrival,
he prostrated with his head at the World-Honored One’s feet and addressed the Buddha, saying:
"By what causes and conditions did the elder Sunetra [become thus]?"
And they shall obtain such vast merit, vast wealth and nobility,
and vast storehouses filled with various goods—
accumulations of millet, wheat, gold, silver, and precious jewels.
"Excellent, World-Honored One! I pray that you will explain this matter for me.
The Buddha told Ānanda:
"This elder Candra has great wisdom."
To be able to give rise to the resolve, maintain it in memory without ever forgetting,
receive, uphold, read, recite, make offerings to, and revere it;
and to contemplate its wondrous principles while giving rise to great compassion.
By expounding this Dharma for the sake of other sentient beings,
you will be able to attain inconceivable and supreme merit,
and throughout immeasurable lifetimes, you shall constantly expound this Dharma for the sake of the devas and the people of the world.
Ānanda, this dhāraṇī is truly unprecedented.
Among all the celestial Māras, the Great Brahmā Kings,
the assemblies of śramaṇas and brāhmaṇas, devas, humans, asuras, and so forth—
Regarding this Auspicious Dhāraṇī for Sustaining the World,
one should always resolve to revere and honor it;
one must not give rise to thoughts of contempt or destruction.
Ānanda, this Auspicious Dhāraṇī for Sustaining the World cannot be destroyed by any other spells.
It is [ineffective] only for those sentient beings who lack roots of goodness or those whose merit is meager.
Their ears cannot hear it for even a moment,
let alone be able to know this dhāraṇī;
how then could they possibly be present within this sūtra?
Whatever one recollects in the mind, proclaims with the mouth, upholds, reads,
and recites— why is this so?
Because this auspicious *Lokadharaṇī* has been proclaimed by all the Tathāgatas together.
It is empowered by all Tathāgatas;
it is unanimously authorized by all Tathāgatas;
it explains, honors, reveres, and praises [it].
This most supreme, subtle, profound, and difficult-to-understand Dharma is proclaimed by all Tathāgatas with a single voice,
their minds being each and every one without distinction.
May all sentient beings attain easy understanding.
For the sake of all sentient beings, I now undergo much poverty and destitution,
the suffering of illness, and various evils and terrors.
All obstructive, vexing, and unpleasant matters shall be made abundant,
secure, and joyful for those who receive [this teaching].
At that time, Ānanda—
Having heard the Buddha preach this Auspicious Dhāraṇī for Upholding the World,
they shall give rise to a mind of mindfulness, receive and uphold it, read and recite it,
contemplate and comprehend it, and honor and make offerings to it.
Ānanda rose from his seat, bared his right shoulder,
knelt with his right knee on the ground, and joined his palms toward the Buddha.
Having thus paid homage to the Buddha, Ānanda then spoke.
With a heart of utmost sincerity, he spoke this *gāthā* and praised [the Buddha], saying:
The Buddha, the World-Honored One, is inconceivable; The Dharma taught by the Buddha is inconceivable.
Inconceivable is the arising of a joyful mind; Inconceivable is the ripening of results experienced in the present life.

The Teacher of Gods and Humans, the Omniscient One, who has reached the further shore and thus transcended birth and death, has realized the unsurpassed fruit and become the Dharma King; I now praise the Buddha’s fearlessness.
At that time, Ānanda, having spoken this praise, [fell silent].
Filled with joy and leaping for gladness, he addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One, what is the name of this sutra?
How should I receive and uphold it?"
The Blessed One said to Ānanda:
"Regarding what you previously asked concerning the householder Sucandra."
This is the Sūtra on the Method for Attaining and Maintaining All Treasuries of Wealth and Jewels.
It is titled "Spoken by All Tathāgatas" and is also known as the *Śrī-lokadhara-dhāraṇī-sūtra*.
"You all should receive and uphold it in this way.
When the Buddha had finished speaking this sutra,
Ānanda, the bhikṣus, and the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas [rejoiced].
All those in the world—gods, humans, asuras, gandharvas, and others—were filled with great joy;
they received and practiced it with faith, paid homage, and withdrew.
Thus concludes the *Mahāyāna Ārya-Śrī-Lokeśvara-Dhāraṇī Sūtra*.
